name: dialog
description: The native dialog element as a modal, opened by a button that names it, with the page behind it inert and focus held inside.

attributes.name: data-width
attributes.description: How wide the dialog may grow.

children.description: The contents: a heading that names the dialog, then whatever it is for.
The buttons, at the end edge. A button inside a form with method="dialog" closes it with no script.

tokens.name: --yeti-dialog-backdrop
tokens.description: The wash over the page behind it.

keyboard.action: Cycles inside the dialog, since the rest of the page is inert.

a11y.notes: Give the dialog a name with aria-labelledby pointing at its heading. Opened with showModal, which is what dialog.js does, the browser makes everything behind it inert, holds focus inside, and closes on Escape; none of that needs ARIA. A button inside a form with method="dialog" closes it without any script. Without the module nothing opens the dialog, so never put the only route to something behind one on a page that does not load it.
